question: Select the correct chemical reaction that represents the chlor-alkali process.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(I) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chlor-alkali process is an industrial method for the electrolysis of sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• This process produces three important products: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), chlorine gas (Cl2), and hydrogen gas (H2).
 
• In this process, an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine) is electrolyzed.
 
• The overall chemical reaction for the chlor-alkali process is: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g).
 
• This process is essential in industries for the production of caustic soda (NaOH) and chlorine, which are used in various applications like soap making, paper production, and water treatment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis Process:**

 
 
• Electrolysis involves passing an electric current through an electrolyte (such as brine) to cause a chemical change.
 
• In the chlor-alkali process, electrolysis occurs in a cell where sodium chloride (NaCl) solution is split into its components.
 
 
 
• **Products of Chlor-Alkali Process:**
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH):** Used in soap making, paper production, and other chemical industries.
 
• **Chlorine Gas (Cl2):** Used in water treatment, disinfectants, and the production of PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2):** Used in the production of ammonia for fertilizers and as a fuel source.
 
 
 
• **Types of Chlor-Alkali Cells:**
 
 
• **Mercury Cell:** Uses mercury as the cathode; however, environmental concerns have led to reduced use.
 
• **Diaphragm Cell:** Uses a diaphragm to separate the products, preventing them from mixing.
 
• **Membrane Cell:** Uses a selective membrane to separate ions, considered the most environmentally friendly.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Chlor-alkali plants must manage the environmental impact of chlorine and mercury emissions.
 
• Modern technologies aim to reduce these impacts, promoting cleaner production methods.
